source.text: Ἐβάστασαν οὖν πάλιν λίθους οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἵνα λιθάσωσιν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Took up therefore again stones the Jews that they might stone him.

en.L: So the Jews again picked up stones in order to stone {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Once more the Jews who had gathered around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} picked up stones to stone {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Then the Jews standing around Jesus picked up stones again. They wanted to stone {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death.

es.L: Los judíos tomaron otra vez piedras para apedrearlo.
es.B: Una vez más, los judíos que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} habían rodeado tomaron piedras para apedrearlo.
es.R: Entonces los judíos que rodeaban a Jesús agarraron piedras otra vez. Querían matarlo a pedradas.

fr.L: Les Juifs prirent donc de nouveau des pierres afin de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} lapider.
fr.B: Une fois de plus, les Juifs qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}entouraient ramassèrent des pierres pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} lapider.
fr.R: Alors les Juifs qui étaient autour de Jésus ont de nouveau ramassé des pierres. Ils voulaient {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} lapider, c’est-à-dire {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tuer à coups de pierres.

sw.L: Basi Wayahudi wakaokota mawe tena ili wampige.
sw.B: Kwa mara nyingine Wayahudi waliokuwa wamemzunguka waliokota mawe ili wampige.
sw.R: Ndipo Wayahudi waliokuwa wamesimama kumzunguka Yesu waliokota mawe tena. Walitaka kumpiga mawe hadi afe.

vi.L: Vậy người Do Thái lại nhặt đá lên để ném đá {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Một lần nữa, những người Do Thái vây quanh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại nhặt đá để ném {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Những người Do Thái đứng quanh Đức Giê-xu lại nhặt đá lên. Họ muốn ném đá cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chết.

ko.L: 그러자 유대인들이 다시 돌들을 들었다. 그분을 돌로 치려는 것이었다.
ko.B: 그분을 둘러싸고 있던 유대인들이 또다시 돌을 집어 들고 그분을 돌로 치려 했다.
ko.R: 그러자 예수 주위에 서 있던 유대인들이 또다시 돌을 집어 들었다. 돌로 쳐서 그분을 죽이려는 것이었다.

pt.L: Então os judeus pegaram outra vez pedras para {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} apedrejar.
pt.B: Mais uma vez os judeus que se tinham juntado em volta {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}} pegaram pedras para apedrejá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}.
pt.R: Então os judeus que estavam em volta de Jesus pegaram pedras de novo. Eles queriam matá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} a pedradas.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the hostile hearers who had gathered around Jesus in the temple at the feast of Dedication (10:24)
alternatives: the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: They are the people who surrounded him in Solomon's colonnade and demanded that he say plainly whether he was the Christ (10:22-24). Their questions sound like those of the authorities (1:19; 8:13), and the leaders may well have been among them, but John does not single them out here. The word names this group of hearers, not the people as a whole: Jesus is himself a Jew (4:9, 22), and so are his disciples and, in 10:42, the many who believe in him.

decisions.choice: picked up stones to stone him: to put him to death on the spot for blasphemy
decisions.reason: Stoning was the law's penalty for blasphemy (Leviticus 24:16), and verse 33 names the charge. "Again" points back to 8:59, where they picked up stones after he said "before Abraham was, I am". Here they react to "I and the Father are one" (10:30). There is no trial; they mean to act at once.

decisions.choice: picked up: lifted, or perhaps went and got
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to lift and carry. It may mean that they had to fetch stones, but John's point is the same either way: they were ready to kill him.

decisions.choice: the Jews who had gathered around him (B); the Jews standing around Jesus (R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the group of hearers of 10:24 (meaning decision m1), not the authorities alone and not the Jewish people as a whole. Balanced and Readable keep the word John wrote, as 8:48 does, and tie it to the people present, so that no reader takes it to mean every Jew.

decisions.choice: They wanted to stone him to death
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the sentence and says plainly that stoning was meant to kill (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: los judíos (L); los judíos que estaban allí / que lo habían rodeado (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the hearers gathered around Jesus in the temple (meaning decision m1), not the authorities alone and not the people as a whole, so no level says "dirigentes".

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level; the imperfect ("cherchaient", "disaient") for attempts and talk that went on
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole passage (10:31-42), as in 1:19. The passé simple ("prirent", "répondit", "crurent") is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Readable uses the passé composé ("ont ramassé", "a répondu"), the past tense French readers speak and learn first. The Greek imperfects of verses 39 and 41 stay imperfect at Literal; Balanced and Readable follow the sense, as the English does.

decisions.choice: les Juifs (L); les Juifs qui l’entouraient (B); les Juifs qui étaient autour de Jésus (R)
decisions.reason: The word names the hostile hearers who had surrounded Jesus in 10:24 (meaning decision m1), not the authorities alone and not the whole people. Balanced and Readable keep the word John wrote and tie it to those present, as the English does; the same holds for verse 33. Readable explains "lapider", a word young readers may not know (m2).

decisions.choice: "그분을 둘러싸고 있던 유대인들" (B); "예수 주위에 서 있던 유대인들" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision takes them as the hostile hearers of 10:24, not named as the authorities, so Balanced and Readable keep "유대인들" and say who they were.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean ("그분", the honorific -시-)
alternatives: deity_pronoun spans as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change (style guide, section 7); recorded once for this passage.

decisions.choice: "ném đá" for lithazō
decisions.reason: "ném đá" is the established Vietnamese term for stoning as a punishment; R adds "cho Ngài chết" as the English R adds "to death".

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πολλὰ ἔργα καλὰ ἔδειξα ὑμῖν ἐκ τοῦ πατρός· διὰ ποῖον αὐτῶν ἔργον ἐμὲ λιθάζετε;

records.literal_gloss: Answered them the Jesus, "Many works good I showed you from the Father; because of which of them work me do you stone?

en.L: Jesus answered them, "Many good works I have shown you from the Father; for which work of them are you stoning {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?"
en.B: Jesus said to them, "I have shown you many good works that come from the Father. Which of those works are you trying to stone {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for?"
en.R: But Jesus said to them, "I have done many good works for you to see. They all came from the Father. Which one of them are you going to stone {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for?"

es.L: Jesús les respondió: «Muchas obras buenas {{plural_you:les|os}} he mostrado de parte del Padre; ¿por cuál de ellas {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:apedrean|apedreáis}}?».
es.B: Jesús les dijo: «{{plural_you:Les|Os}} he mostrado muchas obras buenas que vienen del Padre. ¿Por cuál de ellas {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} apedrearme?».
es.R: Pero Jesús les dijo: «He hecho muchas obras buenas delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Todas vinieron del Padre. ¿Por cuál de ellas {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:van|vais}} a apedrear?».

fr.L: Jésus leur répondit : « Beaucoup de belles œuvres, je vous [les] ai montrées de la part du Père ; pour laquelle de ces œuvres {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} lapidez-vous ? »
fr.B: Jésus leur dit : « Je vous ai montré beaucoup de belles œuvres qui viennent du Père. Pour laquelle de ces œuvres voulez-vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} lapider ? »
fr.R: Mais Jésus leur a dit : « Devant vous, j’ai fait beaucoup de belles œuvres. Elles venaient toutes du Père. Pour laquelle de ces œuvres voulez-vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} lapider ? »

sw.L: Yesu akawajibu, "Kazi nyingi njema nimewaonyesha kutoka kwa Baba; kwa ajili ya kazi ipi kati ya hizo mnanipiga mawe?"
sw.B: Yesu akawaambia, "Nimewaonyesha kazi nyingi njema zinazotoka kwa Baba. Ni kazi ipi kati ya hizo mnayotaka kunipigia mawe?"
sw.R: Lakini Yesu akawaambia, "Nimefanya kazi nyingi njema mkiziona. Zote zilitoka kwa Baba. Ni ipi kati yake mnayotaka kunipigia mawe?"

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu đáp lời họ: "Ta đã cho các người thấy nhiều việc tốt đẹp từ Cha; vì việc nào trong những việc ấy mà các người ném đá {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}?"
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Ta đã cho các người thấy nhiều việc tốt đẹp đến từ Cha. Các người định ném đá {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vì việc nào trong những việc ấy?"
vi.R: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Ta đã làm nhiều việc tốt cho các người xem. Tất cả đều đến từ Cha. Các người sắp ném đá {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vì việc nào trong những việc đó?"

ko.L: 예수께서 그들에게 대답하셨다. "내가 아버지께로부터 [나온] 많은 선한 일을 너희에게 보여 주었다. 그 가운데 어떤 일 때문에 너희가 나를 돌로 치려 하느냐?"
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "나는 아버지께로부터 온 선한 일을 많이 너희에게 보여 주었다. 그 가운데 어느 일 때문에 나를 돌로 치려고 하느냐?"
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "나는 너희가 보는 앞에서 좋은 일을 많이 했다. 그 일들은 모두 아버지께로부터 온 것이다. 그 가운데 어떤 일 때문에 나를 돌로 치려는 것이냐?"

pt.L: Jesus lhes respondeu: "Muitas obras boas eu lhes mostrei da parte do Pai; por qual dessas obras vocês {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} apedrejam?"
pt.B: Jesus lhes disse: "Eu lhes mostrei muitas obras boas que vêm do Pai. Por qual dessas obras vocês estão querendo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} apedrejar?"
pt.R: Mas Jesus disse a eles: "Eu fiz muitas obras boas diante dos olhos de vocês. Todas elas vieram do Pai. Por qual delas vocês vão {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} apedrejar?"

decisions.choice: good: good in the sense of fine, noble, worth admiring
decisions.reason: The word is the one Jesus has just used of himself as "the good shepherd" (10:11, 14): what is good in itself and good to look at. The works are deeds such as the healings of 5:1-9 and 9:1-7, which showed the Father's goodness. The same word comes back in the reply of verse 33.

decisions.choice: from the Father: the works have their source in the Father
alternatives: done on the Father's behalf only
decisions.reason: Jesus does nothing on his own; the Father shows him what he does and gives him the works to complete (5:19-20, 36). In 10:25 he says the works he does in his Father's name testify about him, and in 10:37-38 he will rest his case on them.

decisions.choice: are you stoning me: an act begun but not completed
decisions.reason: The present tense describes what they are in the act of doing: they have the stones in their hands (verse 31) but have not thrown them. The question is pointed: for which good deed are they about to kill him?

decisions.choice: I have shown you: done before your eyes, so that you could see what they mean
decisions.reason: To "show" works is to do them openly as evidence. In 5:20 the Father shows the Son all that he does; here the Son has shown those works to them, and they still refuse to see.

decisions.choice: said to them (B, R); are you trying to stone (B); are you going to stone (R)
decisions.reason: Jesus "answers" what they do, not a question, so Balanced and Readable say "said". The verb form means an act under way (meaning decision m3); Balanced says "trying", Readable "going to".

decisions.choice: I have done many good works for you to see. They all came from the Father.
alternatives: I have shown you many good works from the Father
decisions.reason: Readable splits the clause and says what "shown you" means (meaning decision m4). It keeps the word "works", which recurs in verses 33, 37 and 38.

decisions.choice: les dijo; quieren apedrearme (B); van a apedrear (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: an act begun but not completed (meaning decision m3). "Buenas" as in "buen pastor" (m1).

decisions.choice: belles œuvres (every level)
decisions.reason: The adjective is the one used of "the good shepherd" (meaning decision m1): fine, noble, worth admiring. In French "bonnes œuvres" now means acts of charity, which narrows the sense; "belles œuvres" says that the deeds are good and good to look at. The same words are used in the reply of verse 33.

decisions.choice: "선한 일" (L, B); "좋은 일" (R)
decisions.reason: kalos is good as fine and admirable, the same word as "the good shepherd" (10:11); "선한" keeps the link at Literal and Balanced, and Readable uses the everyday "좋은".

decisions.choice: "아버지께로부터 [나온]"
decisions.reason: Korean cannot attach "from the Father" to a noun without a verb; "나온" is supplied in brackets.

decisions.choice: "Ta" and "các người" for Jesus and his hearers
decisions.reason: Style guide section 6, kept from 10:25 through 10:38.

decisions.choice: "tốt đẹp" (L, B); "tốt" (R) for kalos
decisions.reason: "tốt đẹp" adds the sense of fine and admirable that the meaning decision gives the word.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι· Περὶ καλοῦ ἔργου οὐ λιθάζομέν σε ἀλλὰ περὶ βλασφημίας, καὶ ὅτι σὺ ἄνθρωπος ὢν ποιεῖς σεαυτὸν θεόν.

records.literal_gloss: Answered him the Jews, "For a good work not we stone you but for blasphemy, and because you a man being make yourself God."

en.L: The Jews answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "For a good work we are not stoning {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, but for blasphemy, and because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, who are a man, make {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} God."
en.B: The Jews answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "It is not because of a good work that we are stoning {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. It is because of blasphemy: {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are only a man, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are making {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} God."
en.R: The Jews answered, "We are not stoning {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for doing something good. We are stoning {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} because what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} say is an insult to God. You are only a man, but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are making {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} out to be God!"

es.L: Le respondieron los judíos: «No {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} apedreamos por obra buena, sino por blasfemia, y porque {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, siendo hombre, te haces Dios».
es.B: Los judíos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondieron: «No {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} apedreamos por ninguna obra buena, sino por blasfemia: {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, que no eres más que un hombre, te haces Dios».
es.R: Los judíos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondieron: «No {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} apedreamos por hacer algo bueno. Te apedreamos porque lo que dices es un insulto contra Dios. ¡Tú no eres más que un hombre, pero te haces pasar por Dios!».

fr.L: Les Juifs {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondirent : « Pour une belle œuvre, nous ne {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} lapidons pas, mais pour un blasphème, et parce que {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, qui es un homme, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} fais Dieu. »
fr.B: Les Juifs {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondirent : « Ce n’est pas pour une belle œuvre que nous {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} lapidons, c’est pour un blasphème : {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} n’es qu’un homme, et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} fais Dieu. »
fr.R: Les Juifs ont répondu : « Nous ne {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} lapidons pas parce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as fait quelque chose de bien. Nous {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} lapidons parce que ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} dis est une insulte contre Dieu. Tu n’es qu’un homme, mais {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} prétends être Dieu ! »

sw.L: Wayahudi wakamjibu, "Kwa ajili ya kazi njema hatukupigi mawe, bali kwa ajili ya kukufuru, na kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, uliye mwanadamu, unajifanya {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} Mungu."
sw.B: Wayahudi wakamjibu, "Hatukupigi mawe kwa sababu ya kazi njema. Ni kwa sababu ya kukufuru: {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni mwanadamu tu, {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} unajifanya {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} kuwa Mungu."
sw.R: Wayahudi wakajibu, "Hatukupigi mawe kwa kufanya jambo jema. Tunakupiga mawe kwa sababu unachosema ni kumtukana Mungu. Wewe ni mwanadamu tu, lakini unajifanya {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} kuwa Mungu!"

vi.L: Người Do Thái đáp lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Chúng tôi không ném đá ông vì một việc tốt, nhưng vì sự phạm thượng, và vì ông là người mà tự làm mình thành Đức Chúa Trời."
vi.B: Người Do Thái trả lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Chúng tôi ném đá ông không phải vì một việc tốt, mà vì tội phạm thượng: ông chỉ là người mà lại tự cho mình là Đức Chúa Trời."
vi.R: Người Do Thái trả lời: "Chúng tôi không ném đá ông vì ông làm việc tốt. Chúng tôi ném đá ông vì ông nói những lời xúc phạm Đức Chúa Trời. Ông chỉ là một con người, vậy mà ông dám tự xưng mình là Đức Chúa Trời!"

ko.L: 유대인들이 그분께 대답했다. "선한 일 때문에 우리가 너를 돌로 치는 것이 아니라 신성 모독 때문이다. 네가 사람이면서 스스로를 하나님으로 삼기 때문이다."
ko.B: 유대인들이 그분께 대답했다. "우리가 너를 돌로 치려는 것은 선한 일 때문이 아니라 신성 모독 때문이다. 너는 사람일 뿐인데 스스로 하나님이라고 하고 있다."
ko.R: 유대인들이 대답했다. "우리는 네가 좋은 일을 해서 돌로 치려는 것이 아니다. 네가 하나님을 모욕하는 말을 했기 때문이다. 너는 사람일 뿐인데 스스로 하나님인 척하고 있지 않느냐!"

pt.L: Os judeus {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} responderam: "Por uma obra boa não {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} apedrejamos, mas por blasfêmia, e porque {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}, sendo homem, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} fazes Deus."
pt.B: Os judeus {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} responderam: "Não é por causa de uma obra boa que estamos {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} apedrejando. É por causa de blasfêmia: {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és apenas um homem e estás {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} fazendo Deus."
pt.R: Os judeus responderam: "Não estamos {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} apedrejando por teres feito alguma coisa boa. Estamos {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} apedrejando porque o que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} dizes é um insulto a Deus. Tu és apenas um homem, mas estás querendo passar por Deus!"

decisions.choice: the Jews: the same hearers as in verse 31
alternatives: the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: They answer the question Jesus has just put to them. They are the group who gathered around him in 10:24 and now hold stones (meaning decision on 10:31), not the people as a whole.

decisions.choice: blasphemy: speaking in a way that dishonors God; "and because" says what the blasphemy is
decisions.reason: The law put to death anyone who blasphemed the name of the LORD (Leviticus 24:10-16). The second clause does not add a new charge but explains the first: claiming to be God is, in their view, the blasphemy itself. Jesus repeats their charge in verse 36.

decisions.choice: make yourself God: God, the one God of Israel
decisions.reason: The word has no article, but Greek often leaves out the article with a noun that completes the verb, as here, and the same word without the article means God in 1:1 and 1:18. The charge matches 5:18, where they say he makes himself equal to God, and it answers what Jesus has just said: "I and the Father are one" (10:30). Grammar alone would also allow "a god", and Jesus's reply in verses 34-36 argues from "gods"; a footnote gives that reading.

decisions.choice: you, being a man, make yourself God: their charge, which John's reader sees in a different light
alternatives: a statement John endorses as it stands
decisions.reason: The reader knows from 1:1 and 1:14 that the Word was God and became flesh. So the speakers are right that a man stands before them and wrong about the rest: Jesus does not make himself anything. He does nothing on his own (5:19, 30), and it is the Father who glorifies him (8:54). Compare 5:18.

decisions.choice: It is not because of a good work ... It is because of blasphemy (B); two sentences (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "for a good work" first for emphasis, throwing back Jesus's question. Balanced keeps the emphasis with "It is not ... It is"; Readable uses short sentences.

decisions.choice: what you say is an insult to God; making yourself out to be God
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word "blasphemy" (meaning decision m2) and says "making yourself out to be", which keeps the sense that this is a claim they reject (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: un insulto contra Dios; te haces pasar por Dios
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable explains "blasfemia" (meaning decision m2). "Dios" with a capital: the one God (m3, whose footnote gives the other reading).

decisions.choice: tu te fais Dieu (L, B); tu prétends être Dieu (R)
alternatives: tu te fais passer pour Dieu
decisions.reason: "Se faire Dieu" keeps the Greek verb "make" and the charge that he claims a rank that is not his (meaning decision m4); "Dieu" has a capital because the one God of Israel is meant (m3). "Se faire passer pour" would say that he is pretending, which is more than the Greek says at Balanced; Readable's "prétendre" ("claim") says that the hearers reject the claim, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: The opponents speak to Jesus in the plain style without honorifics ("너", "-다")
decisions.reason: They are about to stone him for blasphemy; the style guide lets open opponents address Jesus without honorifics in such a scene.

decisions.choice: "신성 모독" (L, B); "하나님을 모욕하는 말" (R)
decisions.reason: The older Korean Bible word "참람" is no longer understood; "신성 모독" is the current term, and Readable explains it in plain words.

decisions.choice: "ông" for "you", with no deity_pronoun span, in the accusers' speech
decisions.reason: As in 10:24: those who are about to stone him address him as "ông", a form with no reverent capital.

decisions.choice: "phạm thượng" (L, B); "xúc phạm Đức Chúa Trời" (R) for blasphemia
decisions.reason: "phạm thượng" is the standard legal-religious word; R says plainly what it is, as the English R does.

decisions.choice: estás querendo passar por Deus
decisions.reason: Readable says "querer passar por", to claim to be what one is not in the speakers' eyes, as the English Readable says "making yourself out to be" (meaning decision m4). The reflexive pronoun drops out with the idiom, so the R sentence has one deity_pronoun span fewer than the English.

decisions.choice: your law (SBLGNT)
alternatives: the law, without "your" (a few early manuscripts)
decisions.reason: "Your" is missing from a few early witnesses, among them P45, the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Bezae. Most manuscripts have it, and it matches 8:17 ("your law") and 15:25 ("their law"). The sense is hardly changed. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: your law: the Scriptures as a whole, which you accept as God's word
alternatives: the five books of Moses only
decisions.reason: The words come from a psalm, not from the law of Moses, so "law" here means Scripture in general, as in 12:34 and 15:25 (both citing Psalms) and in Paul (1 Corinthians 14:21, citing Isaiah). "Your" is emphatic, as in 8:17: Jesus argues from the authority his hearers accept. He does not distance himself from it; verse 35 says it cannot be broken.

decisions.choice: Psalm 82:6: "I said, 'You are gods'"; God is the speaker, and those he calls gods are human beings who received his word, probably those entrusted with judging his people
alternatives: Israel as a whole, when it received the law at Sinai
decisions.reason: In Psalm 82 God stands among the "gods" and rebukes them for judging unjustly (82:1-4); then he says, "I said, 'You are gods, sons of the Most High, all of you'; but you will die like human beings" (82:6-7). The words quoted match the Greek Old Testament exactly. Jesus describes those addressed as people "to whom the word of God came" (10:35), which fits human hearers: rulers and judges who gave judgment in God's name (compare Exodus 22:8-9 and Psalm 82:2-4), or, as later rabbinic writings explain the psalm, Israel at Sinai. Because the psalm opens with God standing among the "gods" (82:1), it can also be read as addressed to heavenly beings. The argument in verses 35-36 works on any of these readings.

decisions.choice: Your own law says, does it not (B); In your own law God says (R)
alternatives: Does it not stand written in your law (Literal)
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer yes, which Balanced keeps with "does it not" and Readable turns into a statement. "Own" carries the emphatic "your" (meaning decision m2), as at 8:17. Readable names God as the speaker of "I said" (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: ‘Ustedes son dioses’ / ‘Vosotros sois dioses’
decisions.reason: The psalm speaks to more than one person (meaning decision m3), so the plural "you" takes the reader setting even inside the quotation. Spanish marks the third level of quotation with ‘ ’.

decisions.choice: ¿No dice ...? (B); Dios dice (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the question expects "yes"; Readable states it.

decisions.choice: votre Loi (L); votre propre Loi (B, R), with a capital
decisions.reason: The words come from a psalm, so "Loi" here means Scripture as a whole (meaning decision m2); the capital marks it as the name of the Scriptures, as "la Loi" is for the Law of Moses elsewhere. "Propre" carries the emphatic "your", as "own" does in English.

decisions.choice: “J’ai dit : Vous êtes des dieux”, with the psalm's inner words after a colon and no third pair of quotation marks
decisions.reason: French uses « » for Jesus's words and “ ” for the psalm he quotes; a third level of quotation marks is rare and hard to read, so the words God speaks in the psalm follow a colon and a capital. The same is done in verse 36 for what the hearers say and what Jesus said.

decisions.choice: God's words in the psalm: "Ta đã phán", "Các ngươi là thần" (lowercase "thần")
decisions.reason: God speaking to people uses "Ta" and "các ngươi", the forms of a sovereign speaking down; "phán" is the verb for God's speech. "thần" is lowercase because human beings are called by the title.

decisions.choice: a Lei de vocês; Vocês são deuses
decisions.reason: "Lei" keeps its capital: it names the Scriptures as a whole (meaning decision m2), not law in general. God addresses the "gods" of the psalm in the plural, and the Portuguese has only "vocês" for the plural (style section 4); "vós" would be archaic. "De vocês" makes the owner of the law clear, as "sua" would not.

decisions.choice: an argument from the lesser to the greater
alternatives: a claim that Jesus is a god only in the sense the psalm uses
decisions.reason: If Scripture, which cannot be wrong, could call mere human beings "gods" because God's word came to them, it cannot be blasphemy for the one whom the Father consecrated and sent into the world to call himself the Son of God. Jesus argued the same way in 7:23. The point is not that he is one of the psalm's "gods": he is greater than those who received the word, as the one the Father set apart and sent, and verse 38 goes on to say that the Father is in him and he in the Father.

decisions.choice: he called: God, the speaker of "I said" in the psalm
alternatives: it called: Scripture or the law
decisions.reason: In the psalm God says "I said, 'You are gods'" (10:34), so God is the natural subject. Since the psalm is Scripture, the sense is the same if the subject is taken to be the law.

decisions.choice: the word of God came to them: God spoke to them and gave them his word
decisions.reason: The phrase is the one the Old Testament uses when God speaks to someone: "the word of the LORD came to" Jeremiah or Hosea (Jeremiah 1:2; Hosea 1:1). Here it means God's word addressed to those the psalm calls gods. A reader of 1:1 and 1:14 may sense the contrast between those who received the word and the one who is the Word, but John does not draw it out.

decisions.choice: Scripture cannot be broken: its words cannot be set aside or made void
alternatives: Scripture cannot be fulfilled in part
decisions.reason: The verb means to loosen or undo, and so to annul; John uses it of breaking the Sabbath (5:18) and of the law of Moses not being broken (7:23). Even a single word of Scripture, such as "gods", has to be taken seriously. "The Scripture" here means Scripture as a whole, the same as "your law" in verse 34.

decisions.choice: consecrated: set apart for God and for a task he gives
decisions.reason: The verb means to make holy, that is, to set apart for God. It is used of priests set apart for service (Exodus 28:41; 40:13) and of the prophet set apart before birth (Jeremiah 1:5). Jesus uses it again in 17:17-19, of himself and of his disciples. Here it goes with "sent": the Father set him apart for the mission on which he sent him into the world.

decisions.choice: consecrated: perhaps an echo of the feast of Dedication (10:22)
alternatives: no connection with the feast intended
decisions.reason: The feast of Dedication celebrated the cleansing of the temple and the dedication of its new altar after it had been defiled (1 Maccabees 4:36-59). Spoken at that feast, "whom the Father consecrated" may suggest that Jesus is the one truly set apart for God, as the temple and altar were. The word for the feast is a different one, so the echo is possible but not certain.

decisions.choice: I am the Son of God: the sense of what Jesus has said, not a quotation of a single saying
alternatives: a quotation of words found earlier in this conversation
decisions.reason: In 10:25-30 Jesus has not used these exact words, but he has called God "my Father" and said "I and the Father are one" (10:29-30); compare 5:17-25 and 9:35-37. "Son" has no article, as often with a noun that comes before its verb, but it is a title: the Son of God. The psalm goes on to call its "gods" "sons of the Most High" (Psalm 82:6), which may have suggested the comparison.

decisions.choice: set apart (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Set apart" says plainly what the verb means here (meaning decision m5); "sanctified" and "made holy" suggest moral purity, which is not the point. Readable adds "for his work" to show what he was set apart for, joined to "sent".

decisions.choice: how can you tell him, the one whom the Father set apart ... (B); first person, two sentences (R)
alternatives: do you say of him whom the Father consecrated (Literal)
decisions.reason: The Greek question is indignant, so Balanced says "how can you". Jesus speaks of himself first as "him whom the Father consecrated" and then as "I"; Readable says "me" throughout so that a young reader sees that he is speaking of himself, and puts the setting apart and sending first. It states the "if" clause of verse 35 as a fact, since Jesus grants it from Scripture. It says "insulting God" for "blaspheming", as at verse 33.

decisions.choice: llamó, with no pronoun
decisions.reason: Spanish leaves God, the speaker of the psalm, in the verb (meaning decision m2), so no deity_pronoun span is needed.

decisions.choice: consagró (L); apartó (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: "apartar" says plainly what the verb means here (meaning decision m5); Literal keeps "consagrar", which may echo the feast of Dedication (m6).

decisions.choice: consacré (L); mis à part (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Sanctifier" suggests moral holiness, which is not the point; the verb means to set apart for God and for a task (meaning decision m5). Literal keeps "consacrer", the word for setting apart a priest or an altar, which also lets a reader hear the feast of Dedication behind it (m6); Balanced and Readable say "mettre à part", as the English does.

decisions.choice: ne peut être annulée (L, B); personne ne peut mettre de côté ce que dit l’Écriture (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to undo and so to make void (meaning decision m4). French does not speak of "rompre" (breaking) a text, and "abolir" suggests repealing a law; "annuler" says that its words cannot be set aside. Literal and Balanced set the clause between dashes, since it is an aside in Jesus's argument.

decisions.choice: "거룩하게 구별하여" (L, B); "따로 세우셔서" (R)
decisions.reason: hagiazo here is setting apart for God and for a task; Korean "거룩하게 구별하다" says both, and Readable says it in plain words.

decisions.choice: "깨질 수 없다" (L); "폐기될 수 없다" (B); "아무도 없앨 수 없다" (R)
decisions.reason: lyo is to loose or break; Literal keeps the picture, Balanced uses the legal word for making void, Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: "보내신 나에게" (to me, whom the Father sent) at Balanced
decisions.reason: Korean cannot keep the Greek third person ("him whom") and then switch to "I said" in the same clause without confusion; Balanced makes the reference to Jesus himself explicit, while Literal keeps the open "[이]".

decisions.choice: "biệt ra thánh" (L); "biệt riêng" (B, R) for hagiazō
decisions.reason: "biệt riêng" says set apart for God and for a task; Literal keeps the root "thánh" (holy) of the Greek verb.

decisions.choice: "[Đấng]" for the unstated "him" whom the Father consecrated
decisions.reason: Vietnamese needs a head noun for the relative clause; "Đấng" is the respectful noun for Jesus in his own speech about his mission.

decisions.choice: consagrou (L); separou (B, R); Blasfemas / Estás blasfemando
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "consagrar", which also echoes the feast of Dedication (meaning decision m6); Balanced and Readable say "separar", set apart for a task (meaning decision m5), as "santificar" would suggest moral holiness. The charge quoted inside Jesus's words is addressed to him, so it keeps "tu" ("Blasfemas").

decisions.choice: if I am not doing ... do not believe me: a real test Jesus offers
decisions.reason: Jesus invites them to judge him by his works. The law itself called for testing anyone who claimed to speak for God by what followed (Deuteronomy 18:21-22). In 5:36 he has said that the works the Father gave him testify that the Father sent him.

decisions.choice: believe me: accept what I say as true
decisions.reason: With the person in the dative and no "in", the verb means to believe someone's word, as in 5:46 and 8:45-46. In 10:42 it is "believed in him", trust in his person.

decisions.choice: the works of my Father: the deeds the Father gives him to do and does through him
alternatives: works done to please the Father
decisions.reason: The works are the Father's own (5:17, 19-20, 36; 9:4; 14:10). Jesus does them in the Father's name (10:25), so they show who has sent him.

decisions.choice: my Father's works (B); the condition placed second (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek sentence runs on into verse 38 after a raised dot; Balanced and Readable end it here with a full stop. Readable puts the command first, which reads more simply.

decisions.choice: no me crean
decisions.reason: "Creer a" + person: accept what he says (meaning decision m2), as at 5:46.

decisions.choice: "내 아버지께서 맡기신 일" (the work my Father gave me)
decisions.reason: Korean "아버지의 일" could be read as the Father's business in general; Readable says it is the work the Father gives him to do, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: não me creiam (L); não acreditem em mim (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb here means to accept someone's word, not to trust in his person (meaning decision m2), and "crer em" is kept for that trust (10:42). Literal uses "crer" with the plain object; Balanced and Readable say "acreditar em mim", which in everyday Portuguese means to take someone at his word.

decisions.choice: so that you may know and keep on knowing (SBLGNT)
alternatives: so that you may know and believe (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT repeats the verb "know", first in the aorist and then in the present. Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, have "know and believe" instead, which looks like a change made to avoid the repetition. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: know and keep on knowing: come to recognize it, and then go on understanding it
decisions.reason: The first verb is aorist, the start of knowing; the second is present, knowledge that continues and grows. Jesus hopes that the works will lead them first to see the truth and then to live in it.

decisions.choice: believe the works: accept what the works show, even if you will not take my word
decisions.reason: As in verse 37, the verb with no "in" means to accept something as true. The works are evidence that stands even for someone who does not accept Jesus's words; he says the same to his disciples in 14:11.

decisions.choice: the Father is in me and I in the Father: each dwells in the other
alternatives: the Father and Jesus agree in purpose only
decisions.reason: This explains "I and the Father are one" (10:30) without making the Father and the Son the same person: each is in the other. Jesus says it again in 14:10-11 and prays in 17:21 that his followers may be one in the same way.

decisions.choice: and I in the Father (SBLGNT)
alternatives: and I in him (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "in him", as the King James Version does. The sense is the same. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: come to know, and go on knowing (B); see, and go on seeing more and more (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the same verb twice and show the change of tense (meaning decision m2). Readable says "see", meaning to grasp the truth, and "more and more" for the continuing present.

decisions.choice: believe what the works show, even if you do not believe me
alternatives: even if you do not believe me, believe the works (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: Readable puts the command before the concession and says what believing the works means (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: lleguen a saber y sigan sabiendo (L); llegarán a conocer, y seguirán conociendo (B); verán, y verán cada vez más (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the same verb twice, the start of knowing and knowledge that goes on (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: reconnaître ... continuer à reconnaître (L); en venir à reconnaître ... reconnaître toujours mieux (B); voir ... voir de mieux en mieux (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek repeats one verb, first for coming to know and then for going on knowing (meaning decision m2). French "reconnaître" says "come to see that something is true", which fits a clause with "que"; Literal and Balanced use it twice and show the change of tense with "continuer à" and "toujours mieux". Readable says "voir", as the English Readable says "see". "Croyez les œuvres" (without "en") is believing what they show, as "me croire" is believing his word (m3).
Korean needs an object for "do" and a verb in each half of "the Father in me and I in the Father"; the honorific "계시다" for the Father and plain "있다" for the Son are supplied in brackets.

decisions.choice: "biết và cứ tiếp tục biết" (L); "nhận biết và ngày càng hiểu" (B)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese marks the change from coming to know to going on knowing with "tiếp tục" or "ngày càng", since it has no aspect endings.

ko.L: 그러므로 그들은 다시 그분을 붙잡으려고 하였다. 그러나 그분은 그들의 손에서 벗어나 나가셨다.

pt.L: Então procuravam outra vez prendê-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} saiu da mão deles.
pt.B: Então mais uma vez tentaram prendê-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}, mas {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} escapou das mãos deles.
pt.R: Então eles tentaram agarrar Jesus de novo, mas {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} fugiu deles.

decisions.choice: again they tried: one more attempt like those before
decisions.reason: They have tried to seize him before (7:30, 32, 44; 8:20). The imperfect shows an effort that did not succeed. "So" ties it to what he has just said: his reply has not changed their minds.

decisions.choice: seize: lay hold of, arrest
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the earlier attempts to arrest him (7:30, 32, 44; 8:20). Having failed to stone him, they now try to take him into custody.

decisions.choice: went out from their hand: escaped from their grasp and power
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power or control. John does not say how he got away, as at 8:59. Earlier he has explained why such attempts failed: his hour had not yet come (7:30; 8:20).

decisions.choice: their hand: perhaps an echo of "no one will snatch them out of my hand" (10:28-29)
decisions.reason: A few verses earlier Jesus said that no one would snatch his sheep out of his hand or out of the Father's hand. Now they cannot hold him in theirs. The same word is used, but John does not draw the comparison.

decisions.choice: arrest, slipped out of their hands (B); grab, got away from them (R)
alternatives: seize, went out from their hand (Literal)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "hand" so the reader can see the link with 10:28-29 (meaning decision m4). Balanced uses the natural idiom; Readable says plainly that he escaped (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: de su mano (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "mano" so the reader can see the link with 10:28-29 (meaning decision m4).

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} foi de novo para o outro lado do Jordão, para o lugar onde João estava batizando no princípio, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} ficou ali.
pt.B: Depois Jesus voltou para o outro lado do Jordão, ao lugar onde João tinha batizado nos primeiros tempos, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} ficou ali.
pt.R: Depois Jesus voltou para o outro lado do rio Jordão. Ele foi ao lugar onde João tinha batizado as pessoas no começo, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} ficou ali.

decisions.choice: across the Jordan: east of the river, at Bethany beyond the Jordan (1:28)
decisions.reason: The place where John first baptized is named in 1:28 as Bethany beyond the Jordan, not the Bethany near Jerusalem (11:18). It lay outside Judea, out of reach of those who sought to seize him. From there Jesus will be called back to Judea when Lazarus is ill (11:1-7).

decisions.choice: at first: in the early days of John's work
decisions.reason: John the Baptist later baptized at Aenon near Salim (3:23). The phrase sends the reader back to the beginning of the Gospel, where John testified about Jesus at this very place (1:19-34).

decisions.choice: again: back to where he had been before
alternatives: a second journey of the same kind as one just told
decisions.reason: Jesus was with John beyond the Jordan in 1:28-29; now he goes back to that place.

decisions.choice: stayed: remained for a time
decisions.reason: The verb is the one John uses for remaining in Jesus (15:4-10), but here it has its ordinary sense of staying in a place, as in 1:39 and 2:12.

decisions.choice: Jesus (B, R); the Jordan River, had first baptized people (R)
alternatives: he went away ... beyond the Jordan (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus, since the last verse spoke of his opponents. Readable says the Jordan is a river and that John baptized people, as at 1:28.

decisions.choice: se quedó
decisions.reason: The verb "remain" in its ordinary sense of staying in a place (meaning decision m4), so Spanish says "quedarse", as at 1:39 and 7:9.

decisions.choice: il y resta (L, B); il y est resté (R)
decisions.reason: The verb has its ordinary sense of staying in a place here (meaning decision m4), so every level uses "rester"; "demeurer" is kept for the theological sense of remaining in Jesus (15:4-10), as the French brief for John sets out.

decisions.choice: "làm báp-têm" for baptizō
decisions.reason: "báp-têm" is the Protestant word that goes with the guide's names; "rửa tội" and "phép rửa" are Catholic. The style guide does not list the word. Settled for the whole Bible: Vietnamese follows the Protestant tradition's names and terms (the founder's decision, October 2026; docs/vietnamese-style.md).

decisions.choice: "[sông] Giô-đanh"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese names a river with "sông"; it is bracketed at Literal because the Greek has only the name.

records.literal_gloss: And many came to him and were saying that "John indeed sign did none, all things but as many as said John about this [man] true were."

en.L: And many came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and were saying, "John did no sign, but all that John said about this [man] was true."
en.B: Many people came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. "John did not do a single sign," they said, "but every word John spoke about this man was true."
en.R: Many people came to Jesus. They kept saying, "John never did any signs. But everything John said about this man has turned out to be true."

es.L: Y muchos vinieron a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y decían: «Juan no hizo ninguna señal, pero todo lo que Juan dijo de este era verdad».
es.B: Mucha gente fue a verlo. «Juan no hizo ni una sola señal», decían, «pero todo lo que Juan dijo de este hombre era verdad».
es.R: Mucha gente fue a ver a Jesús. Decían una y otra vez: «Juan nunca hizo ninguna señal. Pero todo lo que Juan dijo de este hombre ha resultado ser verdad».

fr.L: Et beaucoup vinrent à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et disaient : « Jean n’a fait aucun signe, mais tout ce que Jean a dit de celui-ci était vrai. »
fr.B: Beaucoup de gens vinrent à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. « Jean n’a pas fait un seul signe, disaient-ils, mais tout ce que Jean a dit de cet homme était vrai. »
fr.R: Beaucoup de gens sont venus voir Jésus. Ils répétaient : « Jean n’a jamais fait de signe. Mais tout ce que Jean a dit de cet homme s’est révélé vrai. »

sw.L: Na wengi walimjia, wakawa wakisema, "Yohana hakufanya ishara yoyote, lakini yote Yohana aliyosema juu ya huyu yalikuwa kweli."
sw.B: Watu wengi walimjia. "Yohana hakufanya hata ishara moja," walisema, "lakini kila neno Yohana alilosema juu ya mtu huyu lilikuwa kweli."
sw.R: Watu wengi walimjia Yesu. Waliendelea kusema, "Yohana hakuwahi kufanya ishara yoyote. Lakini kila kitu Yohana alichosema juu ya mtu huyu kimekuwa kweli."

vi.L: Và nhiều người đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và cứ nói rằng: "Giăng thật không làm một dấu lạ nào, nhưng mọi điều Giăng đã nói về người này đều là thật."
vi.B: Nhiều người đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ nói: "Giăng không làm một dấu lạ nào, nhưng mọi lời Giăng nói về người này đều đúng."
vi.R: Nhiều người đến với Đức Giê-xu. Họ cứ nói với nhau: "Giăng chưa từng làm dấu lạ nào. Nhưng mọi điều Giăng nói về người này đều đã thành sự thật."

ko.L: 그리고 많은 사람이 그분께 와서 말하고 있었다. "요한은 아무 표적도 행하지 않았지만, 요한이 이 사람에 대하여 말한 것은 모두 참이었다."
ko.B: 많은 사람이 그분께 왔다. 그들은 "요한은 표적을 하나도 행하지 않았지만, 요한이 이분에 대해 한 말은 모두 참이었다" 하고 말했다.
ko.R: 많은 사람이 예수께 왔다. 그들은 이렇게 말하곤 했다. "요한은 표적을 하나도 행하지 않았다. 그러나 요한이 이분에 대해 한 말은 모두 사실로 드러났다."

pt.L: E muitos vieram até {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} e diziam: "João não fez nenhum sinal, mas tudo o que João disse a respeito deste [homem] era verdade."
pt.B: Muitas pessoas vieram até {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}. "João não fez um único sinal", diziam elas, "mas tudo o que João falou sobre este homem era verdade."
pt.R: Muitas pessoas foram até Jesus. Elas diziam: "João nunca fez nenhum sinal. Mas tudo o que João disse sobre este homem se mostrou verdadeiro."

decisions.choice: John did no sign, but his testimony was true: John's work was to bear witness, and that witness is confirmed
decisions.reason: John came to testify about the light, not to be it (1:6-8), and he said he was not the Christ (1:20; 3:28). He did no signs, but what he said about Jesus (1:15, 26-34; 3:27-36) has proved true by what they now see. Jesus said in 5:33-36 that John's testimony was true and that his own works were a greater testimony.

decisions.choice: sign: a deed that points beyond itself to who Jesus is
decisions.reason: The word is John's term for Jesus's mighty deeds (2:11; 20:30-31). The people contrast John, who did none, with Jesus, whose signs they know of.

decisions.choice: were saying: kept saying; on the one hand ... on the other: John did no sign, yet he spoke the truth
decisions.reason: The imperfect shows that this was said again and again among the people who came. The two linked particles set the two halves side by side: no sign, but true testimony.

decisions.choice: they said placed inside the quotation (B); has turned out to be true (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced puts "they said" inside the quotation, as natural English does. Readable says "has turned out to be true", which makes explicit that the people are judging John's words by what they now see (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: decían inside the quotation
decisions.reason: As in English: natural order. "Señal", never "milagro" (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "이분" (B, R); "이 사람" (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek "this [man]" is neutral. These are people who come to Jesus and go on to believe (10:42); at Balanced and Readable Korean gives them the respectful "이분", which the plain "이 사람" would lack in their mouths.

decisions.choice: "표적" (sign) at every level
decisions.reason: The book-wide term (style guide, section 6): a deed that points beyond itself, never "기적" (miracle).

decisions.choice: "dấu lạ" for sign
decisions.reason: The style guide's key term; never "phép lạ" (miracle). "dấu chỉ" is closer to "sign" and is left for a reviewer, as at 2:11.

en.B: And many people there believed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: And many people there believed in Jesus.

vi.B: Và tại đó nhiều người đã tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 많은 사람이 거기에서 그분을 믿었다.

pt.R: E muitas pessoas ali creram em Jesus.

decisions.choice: believed in him: put their trust in his person
decisions.reason: The verb with "in" is John's usual way of speaking of trust in Jesus himself (1:12; 3:16), as distinct from believing what someone says (10:37-38).

decisions.choice: there: a contrast with Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The last word is emphatic. In the temple at Jerusalem his hearers tried to stone and seize him (10:31, 39); in the place where John had testified, many believed. The section closes the public ministry in Jerusalem before the raising of Lazarus (chapter 11).

decisions.choice: many people there (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put "there" next to "many people" and supply "people"; Readable names Jesus.
